01 / THE REASON

An idea can be early
and still be important.

A thought does not need to become a product to matter. Sometimes it is worth keeping because it was yours—and because your future self may see something in it that you cannot see yet.

01 — KEEP THE SPARK

Keep the first spark.

A line, a hunch, a half-built plan. Give it somewhere to live before the day fills up around it.

02 — LET IT BREATHE

Let it incubate.

Some ideas need time without a deadline. Set one aside without asking it to prove its value today.

03 — RETURN WITH CONTEXT

See it with new eyes.

When the date arrives, your old thought comes with a new perspective. Notice what changed—and what stayed.

02 / YOUR PERSONAL VAULT

Give a thought
a future.

Write what you want to remember. Choose when you’d like to see it again. Your encrypted capsule stays in this browser. No account, no sync, no server copy. Export an encrypted backup to move it to another browser.

No feed. No streaks. No pressure to turn every thought into a project. The point is to keep what feels important before you know why.

No account, no sync. A passphrase derives an AES-GCM key in this browser; the app stores encrypted capsules, not readable text. The passphrase is not stored or sent. There is no recovery. Clearing this browser’s storage erases the vault. The date is an in-app boundary, not tamper-proof protection. This experiment has not been independently audited; avoid storing secrets or anything irreplaceable.

03 / A SMALL RITUAL

Simple by intention.

Lock Thought makes space for the idea. What you do with it later is up to you.

STEP 01

Capture

Write down the thought while it is still yours to recognize.

STEP 02

Choose a date

Give yourself a moment in the future to come back with fresh eyes.

STEP 03

Return

When it is time, open the capsule and decide what the idea means now.

04 / THE 2030 IDEA

A vault built around
the value of waiting.

Our future-facing vision is a private, time-locked place for ideas: commit once, let the thought incubate, then return with perspective. This page is the first experiment in that direction.

01 — THE SEAL

A deliberate moment of keeping.

In the full vision, sealing is a promise to let the thought sit untouched. This browser demo is not cryptographic storage and can be changed through browser tools.

02 — THE WAIT

Time gives the idea room.

There is no reliable universal 90-second countdown for an idea. The simple truth is that attention moves on; capturing the thought gives you a way back.

03 — THE RETURN

Perspective is the yield.

Open it later to see what your past self noticed. The value may be in the idea—or in how much you have changed.

THERE IS TIME

Keep the thought.
Let the rest unfold.

Your next good idea might be waiting for you to remember it.
